signature.name: Burj Khalifa
signature.detail: The world's tallest building and Dubai's defining sight, with observation decks offering sweeping views over the city and desert. Book timed tickets online in advance and go near sunset for the best light, though mornings are clearer.

signature.name: Dubai Mall
signature.detail: One of the world's largest malls, packed with shops, dining and the Dubai Aquarium & Underwater Zoo inside. It sits at the foot of Burj Khalifa, so pair the two; evenings are liveliest and the metro stops right at the door.

signature.name: Palm Jumeirah
signature.detail: The famous palm-shaped artificial island lined with beaches, hotels and marinas. Drive or take a taxi across it, and stop at the viewing points for photos of the fronds and the skyline.

signature.name: Dubai Fountain
signature.detail: A choreographed fountain show set in the lake beside Dubai Mall and Burj Khalifa. Shows run in the evening; arrive early to grab a spot along the promenade for the best view.

signature.name: Burj Al Arab
signature.detail: The sail-shaped luxury hotel that became a symbol of modern Dubai. It is best seen and photographed from the nearby beaches; access to the interior is limited to guests and diners.

signature.name: Museum of the Future
signature.detail: A striking torus-shaped building housing exhibits on future technology and design. Book tickets ahead as slots fill up, and allow a couple of hours to explore the floors.

signature.name: The Dubai Frame
signature.detail: A giant picture-frame structure with a glass skywalk linking two towers and views over old and new Dubai. Visit in the late afternoon for cooler temperatures and good light.

signature.name: Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood
signature.detail: A preserved old-town quarter of wind-tower houses, courtyards and narrow lanes along Dubai Creek. Go in the morning to wander quietly, then take an abra across the creek.

stay: Good 3-4* hotel $120-200 a night; luxury much higher
transport: Metro about $1-2 a ride; taxis moderate
